notes: v1 covers prohibited practices (Art. 5), a prioritized Annex III high-risk subset, and limited-risk transparency (Art. 50).
Full Annex III coverage is intentionally deferred — better 8 tested categories than a shallow full list.

rules.summary: AI systems that evaluate or classify people based on social behaviour or personal characteristics, producing a social score leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment, are prohibited.
recommended_controls: Do not deploy; redesign the use case away from social scoring
Document why the prior design was discontinued

rules.summary: AI systems that deploy subliminal, manipulative, or deceptive techniques to materially distort behaviour and cause significant harm are prohibited.
recommended_controls: Do not deploy manipulative interaction patterns
Review UX and model objectives for covert influence

rules.summary: AI systems that exploit vulnerabilities of a specific group due to age, disability, or social/economic situation to materially distort behaviour and cause significant harm are prohibited.
recommended_controls: Remove targeting of vulnerable groups for behavioural distortion
Add safeguards and human review before any similar feature ships

rules.summary: Real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement is prohibited, subject to narrow statutory exceptions not modelled in this ruleset.
recommended_controls: Do not enable real-time remote biometric ID in public spaces without a confirmed legal exception
Seek qualified counsel before any law-enforcement biometric deployment
rules.judgment_call_note: Art. 5(1)(h) has listed exceptions (e.g. searching for certain victims/suspects). v1 treats any affirmative real_time_remote_biometric_id flag in LE/public-authority context as prohibited and flags the exception gap for human review.

rules.summary: AI systems that infer emotions of natural persons in the workplace or education institutions are prohibited, with limited exceptions (e.g. medical/safety) not modelled here.
recommended_controls: Disable emotion inference features in workplace and education deployments
Confirm whether any statutory exception could apply before reconsidering
rules.judgment_call_note: Exceptions for medical or safety reasons are not auto-detected from free-text purpose; flagged for human review.

rules.summary: AI used for recruitment or selection of natural persons — including placing targeted job ads, analysing/filtering applications, and evaluating candidates — is high-risk.
recommended_controls: Establish a risk management system and data governance for the system
Ensure human oversight of ranking/filtering decisions
Keep logs and technical documentation for conformity assessment
Assess bias and discrimination risks in candidate scoring
rules.judgment_call_note: Matching on purpose keywords or job_applicants population is a pragmatic proxy; borderline HR analytics that only aggregate headcount may be over-classified and should be reported via misclassification issues.

rules.summary: AI intended for decisions on promotion, termination, task allocation, or monitoring/evaluating performance and behaviour of workers is high-risk.
recommended_controls: Provide meaningful human oversight of employment decisions
Inform workers about AI use affecting them
Document intended purpose and limits of monitoring

rules.summary: AI used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons or establish their credit score is high-risk (excluding fraud detection uses carved out in the Act).
recommended_controls: Run a conformity assessment appropriate to the credit use case
Ensure transparency of scoring factors to affected persons where required
Monitor for discriminatory outcomes across protected groups
rules.judgment_call_note: Fraud-detection carve-out is not inferred automatically; systems labelled only as fraud detection may still match on financial_credit_data and need a misclassification review.

rules.summary: AI systems intended for biometric categorisation according to sensitive or protected attributes are high-risk (distinct from prohibited real-time remote biometric identification).
recommended_controls: Treat as high-risk biometric system: quality management, logging, human oversight
Minimise sensitive attribute inference; justify necessity
Separate this path clearly from any real-time public-space identification features

rules.summary: AI used by or on behalf of law enforcement to assess an individual's risk of offending or reoffending, or risk to victims, is high-risk (subject to prohibited-practice checks first).
recommended_controls: Apply high-risk obligations for law-enforcement AI
Ensure strict access control and logging
Verify the use is not a prohibited social-scoring or biometric practice
rules.judgment_call_note: Deployment context law_enforcement alone is enough to match in v1 when combined with risk-scoring keywords OR LE data OR suspects population — may over-include admin tooling; track via misclassification reports.

rules.summary: AI used to determine access or admission to education or vocational training institutions is high-risk.
recommended_controls: Human oversight of admission decisions
Bias testing across demographic groups
Clear documentation of decision criteria

rules.summary: AI used to evaluate eligibility for essential private services — including health services and life/health insurance pricing/underwriting in scope of the Annex — can be high-risk.
recommended_controls: Confirm whether the specific service falls under Annex III (5)
Apply high-risk quality and oversight controls if in scope
rules.judgment_call_note: Annex III (5)(c) wording is nuanced; v1 uses a coarse patients/health/insurance heuristic.

rules.summary: Providers of AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons must inform those persons that they are interacting with an AI system, unless obvious from the context.
recommended_controls: Disclose AI interaction to end users at the start of the conversation
Keep disclosure clear and accessible
rules.judgment_call_note: Art. 50 applies more broadly than chatbots; requiring both an interactive autonomy level and chatbot-like purpose keywords may under-detect non-chat interactive systems.

rules.summary: Providers of AI systems generating synthetic audio, image, video, or text content must ensure outputs are marked in a machine-readable format where technically feasible.
recommended_controls: Implement machine-readable content marking where feasible
Document cases where marking is not technically feasible
